key_themes: Middle East escalation (UAE intercepts Iranian missiles) lifts oil, weighs on travel and broad equities
Senate CLARITY Act bipartisan agreement ignites crypto rally — Coinbase, Circle surge
GameStop launches surprise $56B unsolicited bid for eBay; Amazon Supply Chain Services disrupts FedEx and UPS
Heavy earnings week: Palantir crushes Q1 with 85% revenue growth; Pinterest and Tyson also beat

stocks.reason: Shares surged ~10% after GameStop submitted a non-binding proposal to acquire eBay at $125/share ($56B total), a 46% premium to its unaffected price; eBay board acknowledged receipt.
Stock fell ~8.5% as markets questioned the $56B bid for eBay; Ryan Cohen held combative CNBC interview about financing the deal half-cash, half-stock via $20B TD Bank letter and $9.4B cash pile.

Reported Q1 2026 after hours: revenue +85% YoY to $1.63B (beat $1.54B est), U.S. revenue +104%, EPS $0.33 vs $0.28 est; raised FY2026 guidance to $7.65-7.66B (71% growth), crushing consensus of $7.27B.
Jumped ~15% after hours on Q2 revenue guidance of $1.13-1.15B, topping analyst consensus of $1.11B; Q1 earnings beat expectations on both top and bottom lines.

Surged ~16% as Senate reached bipartisan agreement on the CLARITY Act crypto market structure bill, with Coinbase and Circle immediately backing the stablecoin yield compromise; Polymarket odds of passage jumped from 46% to 64%.
Rose ~7% on the bipartisan CLARITY Act stablecoin compromise; CEO Brian Armstrong posted "Mark it up" — Coinbase has been the leading industry advocate for the legislation.

Fell ~5% after HSBC downgraded from Buy to Hold (price target $340), warning the stock's 77% rally since early April has fully priced in upside ahead of Q1 earnings; foundry capacity constraints seen limiting server segment growth.
Fell ~9% as Amazon unveiled Amazon Supply Chain Services — a bundled logistics stack (freight, fulfillment, last-mile) now open to all third-party businesses, threatening FedEx's core business model.

Dropped ~10% alongside FedEx on Amazon Supply Chain Services launch; CEO Carol Tomé noted Q1 U.S. domestic daily volumes already fell 8% from the ongoing Amazon glide-down, compounding investor concern.

Fell ~6.5% after mixed Q1 report: EPS beat (+121% to $0.23) but full-year adjusted EPS guidance slashed to $1.45-$1.79 from prior range, citing Middle East conflict disruptions, higher fuel costs, and softer European bookings.

Stock gained modestly after Q1 2026 results: operating profit +18% to $11.34B under new CEO Greg Abel (first quarter without Buffett); cash pile rose to a record $397.4B, slightly missing operating earnings consensus of $11.56B.

Rose ~3% on fiscal Q2 beat: EPS $0.87 vs $0.78 est; raised annual adjusted operating income guidance by $100M to $2.2-2.4B range; Chicken segment margin hit 11.8% and company reduced gross debt nearly $1B over past year.

Reported Q1 revenue of $2.99B (+8% YoY, slightly below $3.03B est) but EPS beat at $4.47 vs $4.31 est; announced positive Phase 3 interim data from RAINIER study in IgA nephropathy, describing povetacicept as "best-in-class potential."

Reported Q1 EPS of $0.64 (beat $0.62 est) on revenue of $1.51B; AI data center revenue more than doubled YoY; stock traded mixed as revenue slightly missed; Q2 guidance of $1.535-1.635B with expanding gross margins signaled recovery.
